# Pixel Streaming Bridge: tools for AI assistants

<!-- Generated by tools/export-tool-reference.mjs from the running plugin. Do not edit by hand. -->

24 tools, served by the `psb` MCP server 1.1.0 inside the Unreal Editor. An assistant reads the same list from the server itself (`tools/list`); this file is for people.

- Endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:47930/mcp` (or the next free port up to 47939). Run `PSB.Mcp` in the Output Log for the URL, the token and the connect command.
- The same tools run from the console: `PSB.Tools` lists them, `PSB.Tool <name> {json}` calls one; and from Blueprint or Python through `PSBMcpLibrary`.
- Names are `family_verb`; arguments are camelCase. An answer is a short sentence plus structured JSON; a refusal says what to do instead.

## What the server tells the assistant

```text
Pixel Streaming Bridge (PSB) carries JSON messages between a web page and an Unreal app streamed with Pixel Streaming. Every message is an envelope {"version":"1.0","type":"command"|"event","name":"ns.action","payload":{...}}: the web sends commands (it adds a requestId), Unreal answers with events. psb.* is reserved for the bridge; app.* is for the user's own messages. Never rename a wire name a client already sends.
Begin with psb_status, then scene_status. The source of truth is the message manifest (an asset, default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages, or a *.psb.json file): manifest_from_use_case creates the messages of a use case in one go, manifest_put_message adds or replaces one, manifest_import_existing seeds it from TypeScript constants or a docs table, manifest_validate checks it. Fix every error before generating.
From the manifest: gen_json_schema, gen_typescript (constants, payload interfaces, a typed sendCommand for the web app), gen_docs (a commands table), gen_datatable (a DataTable of FPSBMessageRow), or gen_all. Files are only written inside the project directory, when you pass outDir.
In Unreal: bp_create_handler makes a Blueprint that binds every command with BindPSBCommand and calls a Custom Event per command with typed inputs; the user fills those events in. scene_setup_bridge places a PSBBootstrap (or the handler) in the level; scene_launch_args gives the command line for streaming. To test, ask the user to press Play, then scene_send_test_command and scene_list_message_traffic; viewport_screenshot shows the result.
Tools that change assets, the level or settings say so; changes to assets and the level can be undone with Ctrl+Z. Ask the user before manifest_remove_message, before overwriting a Blueprint, and before writing files they did not ask for.
```

## bp

### bp_add_command_handler

**Add a command to a handler Blueprint**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Adds a command of the manifest to an existing handler Blueprint the same way bp_create_handler does (binding in BeginPlay, dispatcher, typed On<Command> event); commands it already handles are skipped. Add the message to the manifest first. Undo with Ctrl+Z.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `blueprint` | string |  | The handler Blueprint (default /Game/PSB/BP_PSBCommandHandler). |
| `command` | string |  | The command's wire name; it must be in the manifest. |
| `commands` | array of string |  | Several commands at once. |
| `save` | boolean |  | Save the Blueprint to disk (default true). |

### bp_create_handler

**Create a command handler Blueprint**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Creates an Actor Blueprint (parent PSBBootstrap by default) that receives the manifest's commands with no wiring left to do: BeginPlay binds each command with BindPSBCommand to a dispatcher event, which reads the payload with typed getters and calls a Custom Event On<Command> whose inputs are the payload fields (String, Float, Integer, Boolean, arrays; objects as JSON text) plus PSBCommand (the payload, for ReplyToCommandJson). The user writes their logic in those On<Command> events. It is compiled and the compile errors, if any, come back. Refuses an existing asset.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `blueprint` | string |  | New Blueprint asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/BP_PSBCommandHandler). |
| `parent` | string: `PSBBootstrap` / `Actor` |  | PSBBootstrap (default: also starts the transport) or Actor. |
| `commands` | array of string |  | Only these commands (default: every command of the manifest). |
| `save` | boolean |  | Save the Blueprint to disk (default true). |

### bp_list_handlers

**List command handler Blueprints**. Reads only: never changes anything.

The command handler Blueprints under /Game (made by bp_create_handler): the commands each binds, whether it compiles, and the manifest's commands it does not handle yet.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |

## gen

### gen_all

**Generate everything**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Writes everything generated from the manifest into outDir (inside the project only): messages.psb.json, schemas/*.schema.json, psb-messages.ts, PSB_MESSAGES.md; and creates or refreshes the DataTable. Refused while the manifest has errors.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `outDir` | string |  | Folder for the files, relative to the project directory (default PSBGenerated). |
| `prefix` | string |  | TypeScript constant prefix. |
| `title` | string |  | Docs title. |
| `dataTable` | boolean |  | Also generate the DataTable (default true). |
| `table` | string |  | DataTable asset path. |
| `save` | boolean |  | Save the DataTable to disk (default true). |

### gen_datatable

**Generate a DataTable**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Creates or refreshes a DataTable with row struct FPSBMessageRow (name, direction, description, fields, response, example payload JSON), one row per message, row name = wire name. Blueprints can look messages up with Get Data Table Row. Undo with Ctrl+Z.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `table` | string |  | DataTable asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/DT_PSBMessages). |
| `save` | boolean |  | Save the asset to disk (default true). |

### gen_docs

**Generate a messages reference**. Reads only: never changes anything.

A Markdown reference like the project's COMMANDS docs: the envelope, a commands table (payload shape, values, response, the Unreal handler the generated Blueprint calls), an events table, one section per message with an example envelope, and the error codes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `title` | string |  | Document title (default PSB Messages). |
| `outFile` | string |  | Also write it to this .md file (relative to the project directory). |

### gen_json_schema

**Generate JSON Schemas**. Reads only: never changes anything.

JSON Schema (2020-12) of each message's full envelope (version, type and name as constants, the payload with its fields, the optional requestId) and one schema for any envelope. Returned inline; written as files only with outDir. Extra payload keys are allowed (clients may send legacy keys).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `name` | string |  | Only this message. |
| `outDir` | string |  | Also write <wire_name>.schema.json files and envelope.schema.json to this folder (relative to the project directory). |

### gen_typescript

**Generate TypeScript typings**. Reads only: never changes anything.

TypeScript for the web app in the style of the PSB web templates: name constants (as const), one payload interface per message, name -> payload maps, the response map, a typed sendCommand wrapper (typed<Prefix>SendCommand(usePSB().sendCommand)) and an event handler type. Writes a file only with outFile; copy it into the web app yourself.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `prefix` | string |  | Constant prefix: APP gives APP_COMMANDS / APP_EVENTS (default: the most common namespace). |
| `outFile` | string |  | Also write it to this .ts file (relative to the project directory). |

## manifest

### manifest_from_use_case

**Create messages for a use case**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Creates every message of a use case in one go. You design the messages from what the user wants (e.g. a configurator: app.set_color {color: enum}, app.set_view {viewId}, event app.state {..}); this tool only adds them, deterministically: bare names get the namespace, all are checked first and nothing is written if any is wrong or already exists (unless replaceExisting).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `namespace` | string |  | Namespace for names given without one (default app). |
| `messages` | array of object | yes | The messages of the use case; a name without a dot gets the namespace. |
| `addReplyEvents` | boolean |  | For each command without a response, also add the event <command>_result {ok, message?}. |
| `replaceExisting` | boolean |  | Overwrite messages of the same names (default false: refuse). |
| `allowReserved` | boolean |  | Allow psb.* names (only to mirror existing ones). |
| `save` | boolean |  | Save the asset to disk (default true). |

### manifest_get

**Read the message manifest**. Reads only: never changes anything.

The message manifest in full (every message with its fields), or one message with `name`. The manifest is the source of truth for the web <-> Unreal protocol: schemas, typings, docs, the DataTable and the Blueprint handlers are generated from it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `name` | string |  | Only this message (its wire name). |

### manifest_import_existing

**Import existing wire names**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Seeds the manifest from what a web client already sends, best effort: TypeScript constants (direction from the const name: *COMMAND* or *EVENT*; field names from 'Payload: { a, b }' comments, types guessed) or a Markdown commands table (types from the payload shape, enums from "a|b" literals; tables under an Events heading become events). Names are kept exactly as found, psb.* and legacy ones included. Reports what was skipped and which field types were guessed.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `source` | string | yes | File under the project directory: a .ts constants file (PSB_COMMANDS / psbCommands / *EVENTS* objects), a .md docs file with a commands table (\| `ns.action` \| `{ "key": type }` \| ...), or a .psb.json manifest. |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | Replace messages already in the manifest (default false: keep them). |
| `save` | boolean |  | Save the asset to disk (default true). |

### manifest_list_messages

**List messages**. Reads only: never changes anything.

One line per message: name, direction, fields (name?: type, ? = optional), response. Use it to see what the protocol already has before adding messages.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `direction` | string: `command` / `event` |  | Only commands or only events. |
| `namespace` | string |  | Only names starting with this namespace, e.g. app. |

### manifest_put_message

**Add or replace a message**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Adds one message to the manifest (creating the manifest if needed), or replaces it with replace=true. A message is {name: 'app.set_color', direction: 'command' (web -> Unreal) | 'event' (Unreal -> web) (or from: 'web' | 'unreal'), description, fields: [{name, type: string|number|integer|boolean|string[]|number[]|object, required, description, enum, min, max}], response: 'app.color_changed'}. Names are lower-case dotted; psb.* is reserved. A name is never renamed: to rename, remove the old message and add the new one, and update every client. Nothing is saved if the manifest would have an error.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `message` | object | yes | A message. |
| `replace` | boolean |  | Overwrite the message of the same name (default false). |
| `allowReserved` | boolean |  | Allow a psb.* name, only to mirror one a client already sends. |
| `allowNonStandardName` | boolean |  | Allow a name that is not lower-case dotted, only to mirror one a client already sends. |
| `save` | boolean |  | Save the asset to disk (default true). |

### manifest_remove_message

**Remove a message**. **Destructive**: removes data; the assistant should ask you first.

Removes one message from the manifest. Clients that still send it will get COMMAND_NOT_FOUND unless something else handles it. Ask the user first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |
| `name` | string | yes | Wire name of the message to remove. |
| `save` | boolean |  | Save the asset to disk (default true). |

### manifest_validate

**Validate the manifest**. Reads only: never changes anything.

Checks the manifest: duplicate names, characters a wire name cannot carry, reserved psb.* names (warning), non-standard names (warning), field types, enums only on strings, min/max only on numbers, responses that must be events, missing descriptions. Errors must be fixed before generating.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  | The manifest asset under /Game (default /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages). |
| `file` | string |  | Work on a *.psb.json manifest file instead of the asset: a path relative to the project directory. |

## status

### psb_status

**Pixel Streaming Bridge status**. Reads only: never changes anything.

Start here. Says which Unreal project and level this editor has open, whether a Play-In-Editor session is running, the engine version, and which tool families Pixel Streaming Bridge offers (the part of a tool's name before its first underscore). Read tools/list for the tools themselves.

No arguments.

## scene

### scene_launch_args

**Launch arguments for streaming**. Reads only: never changes anything.

The command-line arguments for running this project with Pixel Streaming locally (-RenderOffScreen, -PixelStreamingURL, -PixelStreamingIP/-Port, -ResX/-ResY ...), a standalone command line from this editor and one for a packaged build. Returns text only: it never launches anything.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip` | string |  | Signalling server host (default 127.0.0.1). |
| `port` | integer |  | Signalling server streamer port (default 8888). |
| `resX` | integer |  | Width (default 1920). |
| `resY` | integer |  | Height (default 1080). |
| `offscreen` | boolean |  | Render off screen, no window (default true). |

### scene_list_message_traffic

**Recent message traffic (Play-In-Editor)**. Reads only: never changes anything.

While Play-In-Editor runs: the latest envelopes in and out of the PSB subsystem, oldest first, each with a note on what became of it (which handler took it, the psb.error it raised, whether the transport sent it). The log keeps UPSBSettings::TrafficHistorySize entries.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer |  | At most this many (default 20). |
| `direction` | string: `in` / `out` |  | Only inbound or only outbound. |
| `name` | string |  | Only names containing this. |

### scene_send_test_command

**Send a test command (Play-In-Editor)**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

While Play-In-Editor runs: feeds a command envelope into the PSB subsystem exactly as if the web client had sent it, and reports what happened: handled by the bridge, a C++ handler, BindCommand handlers or OnCommandReceived listeners, or rejected with which psb.error code and field, plus every envelope that went out in response. Runs the game's handlers, so it can change the running game.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The command's wire name. |
| `payload` | object |  | The command's payload. |
| `requestId` | string |  | Correlation id (default mcp-test-<n>). |

### scene_setup_bridge

**Set up the bridge in the level**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Makes the open level ready: places a PSBBootstrap (the plugin's BP_PSBBootstrap by default, or actorClass=PSBBootstrap for the native one, or a handler Blueprint from bp_create_handler) unless one is there, adds a PixelStreamingInput component if it lacks one, sets the bootstrap's manifest, and applies the given PSB settings (autoStartTransport, autoStartWithoutBootstrap, bindInputHandlers, validateAgainstManifest; manifest also sets DefaultManifest). Level changes are one undoable step; settings go to DefaultGame.ini.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actorClass` | string |  | BP_PSBBootstrap (default), PSBBootstrap, or a /Game Blueprint path. |
| `manifest` | string |  | A manifest asset to load at runtime, e.g. /Game/PSB/PSB_Messages. |
| `addInputComponent` | boolean |  | Add a PixelStreamingInput component if missing (default true). |
| `autoStartTransport` | boolean |  | Project setting: a PSBBootstrap starts the transport on BeginPlay. |
| `autoStartWithoutBootstrap` | boolean |  | Project setting (opt-in): packaged and standalone games also start the transport after a map loads without a PSBBootstrap; PSB then takes over Pixel Streaming Input's UIInteraction events. Left as it is unless given. |
| `bindInputHandlers` | boolean |  | Project setting: receive Pixel Streaming input in C++. |
| `validateAgainstManifest` | boolean |  | Project setting: check inbound payloads against the manifest. |

### scene_status

**Bridge status in the level**. Reads only: never changes anything.

Whether the level is ready for Pixel Streaming Bridge: the Pixel Streaming plugin, the PSBBootstraps in the level (and whether they have a PixelStreamingInput component, a manifest, a Blueprint that sends responses), the PSB project settings, and, while playing, the live subsystem (transport, bound commands, manifest). Ends with next steps.

No arguments.

## settings

### settings_get

**Read PSB settings**. Reads only: never changes anything.

The Pixel Streaming Bridge project settings with what each does: auto-start, input binding, raw messages, who sends responses, traffic log size, the runtime manifest and payload validation.

No arguments.

### settings_set

**Change PSB settings**. Changes something: the assistant's client may ask you first.

Changes Pixel Streaming Bridge project settings (an explicit allow-list; see settings_get) and saves them to DefaultGame.ini. All values are checked before any is changed. Applies from the next Play.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | object | yes | Setting name -> new value, e.g. {"bValidateAgainstManifest": true, "DefaultManifest": "/Game/PSB/PSB_Messages"}. Names as settings_get lists them. |

## viewport

### viewport_screenshot

**Screenshot the viewport**. Reads only: never changes anything.

The level viewport (or, while Play-In-Editor runs, the game's viewport) as a PNG image you can look at: use it to check what a command did to the scene.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxWidth` | integer |  | Scale down to at most this width (default 1280). |
| `play` | boolean |  | While playing, capture the game rather than the editor viewport (default true). |
